name: abandoned rusty box van lying east-west seen from above: long flat roof top, cab windshield, side with sliding door and flat tyres
label: wasteland_ruins/van-rust

surfaces.part: roof vent / hatch and rust patches
south side panel with sliding door and wheels

answer.evidence: The roof is a wide light-grey band at rows 2-17 (width grows from 45 to 64). It carries a vent and rust patches. A darker 1-row front-edge line at row 18 (L=121 at x=32 and x=47) ends the roof. Below it is the south side face at rows 19-26, with a sliding door (dark brown, rows 20-25) and rust streaks. Wheels and tyres sit at rows 25-28 where the silhouette narrows to 18 and 14. The roof band is far larger than a rim, and the side face is more than 3 rows, so it reads as a top surface plus a front face, not a flat slab.

styleAnswer.evidence: The measured facts put the candidate at 19 visible tones per 16x16 tile. That sits level with the stall (17) and well (20) and well above the hedge (9). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so the large roof and side areas are not flat fills. The roof and side panels carry rust patches, speckle and panel seams in several lightness steps. I count about 5 steps on the body ramp, against 5-6 on the references. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline leans toward dark brown or rust beside the material rather than a black sticker line, and forms are often separated by value. The window glass, door seam and tyres are shaded separately from the body. It is slightly less crisp than the roofed well, but a careful artist would accept it next to these references without it looking thinner or flatter.

The eave shadow is weak or absent, and the edge line alone is enough for evidence (a).
